name: An installation can accept bound keys only
aliases: an authorized_keys line without a project or a principal is refused
summary: One installation setting: deployment.private.json's bound_keys_only, absent or false meaning off, so a bare installation is unchanged. admin.py bound-keys-only status|on|off --actor OPERATOR [--file FILE] is operator-gated, holds the deployment config lock, writes nothing when nothing changes, and appends to bound_keys_only_audit, keeping the last 20 flips. status reports audit_agrees and would_be_refused - the lines of this kit and root the setting refuses, or would refuse while off - and on prints that list. With it on, ssh_forced_command.py reads the runtime's own settings file (at most 1 MiB) and refuses, before selecting or running anything, a line naming no --project or no --principal: exit 2, the missing part named, nothing run; a line naming both runs as before. A settings file that cannot be read refuses every forced-command key, saying the installation setting could not be read (no path or value to the contributor); a non-bool value reads as off with a flushed warning. setup-status reports a bound_keys_only block; authorized-keys refuses to print a line the setting would refuse; authorized-keys-list flags such lines and names other-kit or other-root lines as not reached.
